title: Fermentation and Krebs Cycle Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Bread dough puffs up, a tub of batter rises overnight, and your legs burn after a sprint. Diya asks: where do the bubbles come from, and what does a cell do with pyruvic acid when oxygen runs short?

We follow the two paths of pyruvic acid, see alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation with their enzymes, and why fermentation is a poor deal. Then we zoom from a cell into a mitochondrion and its matrix to watch pyruvic acid become acetyl CoA, and run the Krebs cycle step by step. Then the balance for one pyruvic acid, fermentation and aerobic respiration side by side with a pause and think, a worked example for one glucose, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 88 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
